To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we found that biomarkers commonly used in breast cancer research can reliably be used on archival tissue samples up to 60-years old, which will allow us to study how breast cancers have changed over time.
we found excellent reliability for 7 breast cancer biomarkers in formalin-fixed parraffin-embedded (FPPE) breast cancer tissue samples up to 60 years old.
we found that biomarkers commonly used in the diagnosis and management of breast cancer can be reliably assessed in archival tissue specimens up to 50 years old.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel approach for the detection of breast cancer biomarkers.
the long-term trends of biomarkers in breast cancer.
the feasibility of obtaining and analyzing archival FFPE specimens to determine long-term trends in biomarkers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the biomarkers examined are stable over time, and the results obtained are reproducible and reliable.

this is the first study to show that immunohistochemical biomarkers can be reliably assessed in breast cancer specimens from the past 60 years, and that this is an important and necessary step toward the study of long-term trends in biomarkers in breast cancer.

this study is a feasibility study, which shows that it is possible to obtain and analyze archival FFPE specimens of breast cancer diagnosed between 1940 and 2000 for the purpose of determining long-term trends in biomarker expression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
biomarker expression is relatively stable over time, and this may be a reflection of the stability of the underlying tumor biology.
biomarker analysis on archival tissue is a feasible method of obtaining long-term trends in biomarker expression, and thus tumor biology, in breast cancer.

it is possible to reliably analyze biomarkers from archival FFPE breast tumor specimens, even those that are decades old, for the study of historical trends in biomarker expression and tumor behavior, and for the study of the impact of environmental exposures on tumor behavior.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is feasible to study long-term biomarker trends in breast cancer.
the use of FFPE specimens from decades ago can be an important tool for studying breast cancer biology and the impact of treatment on tumor biology over time.
long-term trends in breast cancer tumor biomarkers are now possible to study.
